newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs sag, hit by Brazil fears.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - LatAm ADRs sag, hit by Brazil fears.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) for Latin American companies largely fell Tuesday, weighed by worries that Brazil's currency might come under attack by speculators, traders said.
"It's the jitters about the Brazilian market that's hitting things," one said.
Telecommunications companies, considered the bellwethers of Latin American stocks, stood out among the falling ADRs.

Brazil's state-run Telebras was off 6-1/4 to 139-3/4 in very heavy trade, and Telefonos de Mexico fell 1-1/16 to 51-15/16. Venezuela's CANTV was off 2-1/4 to 42-1/4 and Telefonica de Argentina fell 1-1/4 to 37.
Hinting at the broadness of the downturn, some Latin American mutual funds joined Telebras and CANTV among the New York Stock Exchange's percentage-loss leaders.
The Latin American Discovery Fund was off 1-2/16 to 19-13/16 and Latin American Equity Fund Inc fell 14/16 to 17-7/16.

Traders and analysts said Brazilian ADRs had been weighed by worries that turmoil over Asian currencies, such as the Thai baht and Malaysian ringgit, could hit Brazil. The resulting spillover had swamped Latin American markets.

Brazil, Latin America's biggest economy, has faced stubborn and large current account and trade deficits. Some investors fear that Brazil's currency could be the target of speculative attacks such as those seen in Asia and threaten its economic reform plan.
"I think the main thing is the worries from Asia, really," said Ronald Ratcliffe, chief Latin American economist at Societe Generale in New York.

He noted Brazil's parallels with Thailand, which recently devalued the bhat. Besides the deficits, Brazil's currency, the real, is widely seen as overvalued, its exports are weak and it has a tight monetary policy.
"If Brazil gives up on the (reform) plan ... then you would have two things happen," he said.
"All the other (regional) countries would be less competitive (against Brazilian exports) and then you would have the effect of people not wanting to put money in, or lend."

Among other ADRs, French-Italian semiconductor maker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV rose 3-5/16 to a 12-month high of 88-7/16. Analysts said the ADR had been boosted by the recent recovery of U.S. semiconductor shares.
Oil stocks eased. France's Elf Aquitaine fell 8/16 to 54-9/16, Spain's Repsol dropped 13/16 to 42-11/16 and Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was off one to 53-5/8.
